title: Go
label: Go
desc: Statically typed language with garbage collection and lightweight concurrency.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Create a module, then build, vet, and test the package

snippets.code:
# Name the module after the import path it will serve
go mod init example.com/greet

# Run the main package in the current directory
go run .

# Build a binary called greet into bin/
go build -o bin/greet .

# Report suspicious code without executing it
go vet ./...

# Rewrite files into canonical formatting
gofmt -w .

# Fail the check when any file still needs formatting
test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"

# Run every test in the module
go test ./...

sections.title: Modules
sections.description: One go.mod per module; dependency versions live there

snippets.code:
module example.com/inventory

go 1.22

require golang.org/x/text v0.14.0

# Record a dependency at a chosen version
go get golang.org/x/text@v0.14.0

# Drop requirements that nothing imports any more
go mod tidy

# List the modules used by the current build
go list -m all

# Point a dependency at a local checkout while developing
go mod edit -replace golang.org/x/text=../text-fork

sections.title: Types
sections.description: Primitive kinds, zero values, and explicit conversions

snippets.code:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var count int = 7 // platform-sized signed integer
	var ratio float64 = 0.75
	var initial byte = 'G' // byte is an alias for uint8
	var symbol rune = '世'  // rune is an alias for int32
	var active bool = true

	fmt.Println(count, ratio, initial, symbol, active)
}

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
)

type Level int

const (
	Low    Level = iota // 0
	Medium              // 1
	High                // 2
)

func main() {
	var zero int
	var empty string
	fmt.Printf("%d %q\n", zero, empty) // 0 ""

	small := 300
	truncated := uint8(small) // wraps around: 44
	fmt.Println(truncated)

	text := strconv.Itoa(42) // int to string
	n, err := strconv.Atoi("17")
	fmt.Println(text, n, err, High)
}

sections.title: Common Errors
sections.description: Nil maps, aliased slices, shadowed variables, and typed nils

snippets.code:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	base := []int{1, 2, 3, 4}
	part := base[:2]
	part = append(part, 99) // writes into base's backing array
	fmt.Println(base)       // [1 2 99 4]

	safe := append([]int(nil), base[:2]...)
	safe = append(safe, 100)
	fmt.Println(base, safe)
}
